title: graphty recipe member, version 1
description: A journal of analysis commands -- filters, algorithm runs and a layout -- replayed on any graph whose import has the columns it names (recipe.md). Normative for what a writer produces. The members of each known command, and of its scope and style, are closed: a reader skips a command with a member it does not know, and every command after it (recipe.md, 'Replaying'). op is an open list: a command of a later op is valid, and a reader stops the replay there.

id.description: The recipe's identity across all its versions. A reverse-domain name (org.example.hub-genes) or an https: URL is recommended, so two authors do not collide. Ids starting graphty. or graphty: in any case, and URLs on graphty.app, are reserved for the recipes graphty-element ships.

recipeVersion.description: One version of the recipe, as a SemVer 2.0.0 version.

namespace.description: The namespace this recipe's run ids prefer when it is applied (recipe.md, 'Run ids and namespaces'). Letters, digits and single underscores, so a namespaced run id needs no quoting in a path.

directed.description: The direction of the graph the recipe was recorded on. A replay on a graph of the other direction is reported (recipe.md, 'Binding to a new graph' rule 5).

parallelEdges.description: Whether the graph the recipe was recorded on held more than one edge between a pair of nodes. false makes a replay on a graph that does hold them report it before anything runs (recipe.md, 'Binding to a new graph' rule 5).

delimiter.description: The character that separates columns; the importer's own detection when absent.

variant.description: The CSV shape, as graphty-element's catalogue names it (edge-list, node-list, ...). Never used for the endpoints of a neo4j-variant file, whose header types its own structure.

repeatedEdges.description: What a second edge between the same two nodes becomes.

table.description: For data read from a table (CSV): how it is read, by the import option names of container.md, 'Import options' -- the columns holding an edge's two ends and a node's id, the delimiter, the CSV shape and what repeated rows become. Defaults for a table imported for this recipe through its application's import() or as the file's own data member; the caller's options win, and the endpoint columns, delimiter and variant are used only when the file's first line holds the recipe's endpoint columns (recipe.md, 'Table data'). Ignored for formats that mark endpoints themselves.

generator.description: The release that recorded the recipe. recipes.record() writes it; a replay on another release is reported (recipe.md, 'Same data, same results').

command.description: Dispatched on op, so a validator reports only the errors of the command kind named.

tableColumn.description: A column name, looked up as a plain name, never evaluated.

predicate.description: A predicate in graphty-element's expression language (style.md, 'Expressions') over the table 'on' names: columns as data.<column>, earlier results as results.<as>.<field>. Reads columns only: the structural paths of style.md, 'Paths' rule 4 are refused.

on.description: nodes (the default): keep the matched nodes and the edges between them. edges: keep the matched edges; every node stays unless dropIsolated.

dropIsolated.description: Also drop every node left with no edge once this filter's rule has applied, including one that had none before. Default false.

graphFilter.description: Narrows the graph every later command of the recipe sees, and shows it as the session's filter (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 13).

as.description: The run's name in this recipe. Unique within the recipe; letters, digits and single underscores, never two underscores in a row, which separate a namespace from a name, so a path naming the run needs no quoting. Its meaning never changes between recipe versions.

params.description: Option values by the option names graphty-element's catalogue publishes for the algorithm or layout. An option of type attribute or partition may instead name an earlier run's result as {"result": "<as>.<field>"} (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 4).

on.description: Which table the predicate is evaluated on. nodes (the default): the run sees the matched nodes and the edges between them. edges: the run sees every node and only the matched edges.

description.description: Why this command is in the recipe. Shown to people; never sent to the algorithm.

algorithm.description: An algorithm key from graphty-element's catalogue, or one a plugin registered.

seed.description: The run's seed. Its maximum is the smallest seed range among graphty-element's algorithms. Absent: the algorithm's published default seed, or one drawn at run time when it has none (recipe.md, 'Commands' rule 7).

recordedCapSeconds.description: Advisory: the per-command cost cap the run was recorded under, when it was above the default. A replay never raises its cap from it; the report quotes it beside E_CAP_EXCEEDED so the person replaying knows what to pass (recipe.md, 'Running' rule 2).

recordedPrecision.description: Advisory: the precision the run was recorded in, from its caveats. A replay in the other precision is reported (W_PRECISION_DIFFERS); it never asks for a precision.

style.description: What the run paints when it completes: the run's RunStyle, as graphty-element's run option of the same name. true or absent, the colouring its result suggests; false, nothing.

id.description: A layout id from graphty-element's catalogue, or one a plugin registered.

engine.description: The engine that draws the layout; the catalogue's default engine for id when absent.

options.description: The engine's options, by the names the catalogue publishes, the seed among them.

laterCommand.description: A command a later release adds: a lower-case dotted op, so a misspelling such as algo.Run or algorun is refused here. A version 1 reader skips it and every later command with E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND. A later command that names its result does so in as, as algo.run does.
